falsifier: Any block in which MWCC 1.2.5 emits a fresh `li rD,<K>` for the SECOND of two same-valued constant initialisers while serving the FIRST from a copy, with no intervening call, branch target or clobber. Concretely for the origin site: re-transpose case 17's two initialisers in src/game/audio/dcsdrv.c and read `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/audio/dcsdrv dcsHandleRequest 0x1d8:0x1f8 --diff`; if the fresh `li` does NOT follow the first-written variable, this law is wrong. Independently: a case where transposing the two initialisers changes the NUMBER of `li` instructions (rather than only which register receives the fresh one) would refute the count-neutrality clause.

value:
REFINEMENT, NOT REFUTATION, OF claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source.20260831.v1, whose scope sentence is exactly this situation ('a loop preheader that initializes two induction variables'). THAT LAW IS RIGHT THAT WHETHER A COPY HAPPENS AT ALL IS THE ALLOCATOR'S CHOICE AND IS NOT SOURCE-REACHABLE. What it does not say, and what is measured here, is that WHICH OF THE TWO REGISTERS RECEIVES THE FRESH MATERIALISATION IS DECIDED BY C STATEMENT ORDER: the FIRST-WRITTEN variable gets the fresh `li rD,K` and the SECOND-WRITTEN is served by a register copy from it. Transposing the two initialisers therefore RELOCATES the copy rather than removing it, is exactly instruction-count-neutral, and is a real lever whenever the target and our build disagree about WHICH register the copy lands in.

THE MEASUREMENT. game/audio/dcsdrv::dcsHandleRequest, case 17's preamble, three words at [0x1e0,0x1ec). Source `index = 0;` then `output[0] = resultOffset = 0;` produced
  li r31,0 / addi r30,r31,0 / stw r30,0(r29)
(index, written first, took the fresh `li`; resultOffset copied). Transposing the two lines to `output[0] = resultOffset = 0;` then `index = 0;` produced
  li r30,0 / stw r30,0(r29) / mr r31,r30
(resultOffset, now written first, took the fresh `li`; index copied). The retail target is
  li r28,0 / stw r28,0(r30) / li r31,0
i.e. two independent materialisations, which NEITHER order reproduces - consistent with the parent law, because the count of copies is the allocator's and stayed at one in both orders.

WHY THE TRANSPOSITION IS STILL WORTH TAKING, and this is the operationally important half. The copy's POSITION decides how the streams ALIGN, and alignment decides how many words are OPCODE-class versus register-field-class - which is what governs postprocessor candidacy. Before: `wf_word_diff` read 'DIFFERING WORDS = 67, MNEMONIC DIVERGENCE = 2 ... DECODE: REGFIELD-ONLY 65, IMMEDIATE 0, BRANCH 0, OPCODE 2' and `fndiff --ops` showed TWO MISALIGNED clusters (an inserted `addi` at ours+0x1e4 against a deleted `li` at target+0x1e8). After: 'DIFFERING WORDS = 67, MNEMONIC DIVERGENCE = 1 ... DECODE: REGFIELD-ONLY 66, IMMEDIATE 0, BRANCH 0, OPCODE 1' and ONE ALIGNED `replace`. One word moved from the OPCODE class into the register-field class and the streams re-aligned, taking fresh objdiff fuzzy from 98.6618% to 99.0024%.

TWO ARBITRATION TRAPS THIS SITE DEMONSTRATES, both measured. (1) `real` ROSE 144 -> 146 on the improving edit, and defake_gate's STRUCTURE arbiter also called it a REGRESSION ('genuine structural rows 0 -> 1'). regnorm scored the misaligned BEFORE state as 0 structural rows because that region contained UNPAIRED instructions, which is precisely the configuration AGENTS.md residual-work discipline 3 warns makes positional pairing fabricate (or here, erase) rows. When a copy-vs-remat transposition re-aligns a stream, arbitrate on fresh objdiff fuzzy and on the wf_word_diff DECODE breakdown, and bank with `defake_gate.py check <unit> --bank-arbitrated=<fn>`. (2) The raw differing-word COUNT was flat at 67 across the edit while the OPCODE/REGFIELD split moved - the count is an obligation size, not a distance (claim.law.MC_the-raw-differing-word-count-is-an-obligation-size-not-a-distance-and-must-never-be-differenced-across-probes), so read the DECODE line, not the total.

BOUNDARY, measured at the same site so the lever is not over-generalised: only the ORDER reaches this decision, not the statement SHAPE. Two further probes returned NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL with object hash 7ed3491299bf, i.e. byte-identical objects, so the construct folded away before codegen in both cases: (a) rewriting `index = 0; while (...)` as `for (index = 0; ...;)` - the for-init and the standalone assignment are the same construct to MWCC; (b) unchaining `output[0] = resultOffset = 0;` into `resultOffset = 0; output[0] = resultOffset;`. A third probe moving `resultOffset`'s DECLARATION from first to last in the local list DID reach codegen (real 146 -> 184), so declaration order is a live but differently-aimed lever at this site. Do not spend probes re-spelling the statement; transpose it or leave it.
